solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Book we can parade about

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boastful line from someone who can stage a grand parade for a book launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal: the eleven letters of WE CAN PARADE are rearranged into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's famous novel is a book, so the bare word book stands in for the title.

clue.text: Check rare tins for damage

indicators.note: the words rare tins are to be damaged, that is knocked out of shape and reordered

explanation.surface: An inspector checks some uncommon tins to see whether they have been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for damage' suggests an inspection; 'damage' is the anagram signal on RARE TINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Footballer's action blocked by normal activity at Scottish club

indicators.note: the first piece is blocked, i.e. stopped up in the middle, by the second

parts.note: a footballer's basic action is to kick the ball

indicators.note: activity means the word normal is set in motion, its letters stirred up

explanation.surface: A footballer's kick is stopped by routine play at a Scottish football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activity' stirs up the letters into LMARNO, and 'blocked by' splits the kick to hold them; the surface hides that the club is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilmarnock FC is a Scottish professional football club from the Ayrshire town of that name.

clue.text: Film judge apparently weighing shrunken heads

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters of the four words that come before it

explanation.surface: A film shows a judge seemingly weighing shrunken heads, a gruesome courtroom scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrunken heads' reads as a grisly object; 'heads' takes the first letters of judge, apparently, weighing and shrunken.
explanation.definitionFit: Spielberg's 1975 shark thriller is one of the best-known films ever made.

clue.text: U-boats surprisingly come on shore in African monarchy

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters of the U-boats turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: to come on shore is to land

explanation.surface: German submarines unexpectedly come ashore in an African kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges U-BOATS into BASUTO.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the colonial name of the southern African kingdom now called Lesotho, a monarchy.

clue.text: Note about the French jumper

indicators.note: about says the note goes around the next piece

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A note about a French jumper, as if describing a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, as in British English, but it is an insect that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny insect is famous for leaping huge distances, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Somewhat threatening and hideous Indian politician

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a menacing, ugly politician from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement, and Indira and Rajiv Gandhi were prime ministers.

clue.text: Monk overthrows puritans

indicators.note: overthrows means the word puritans is turned upside down and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A monk topples a group of puritans from power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian mystic who held sway at the Romanov court was a wandering monk, or starets.

clue.text: States things in camera, upsetting authoritarian leader

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over the letters of in camera into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Things discussed privately upset an authoritarian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' here is the United States, not a verb; 'upsetting' rearranges IN CAMERA and 'leader' takes A from authoritarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects and artefacts typical of American culture are collectively called by this name.

clue.text: Everyone backs Massachusetts wool producer

indicators.note: backs means the word for everyone runs backwards

parts.note: everyone means all
MA is the US postal abbreviation for Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Everybody supports a wool producer from Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reads as support, but it reverses ALL to LAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal is kept for its fleece, which is spun into wool.

clue.text: Tiny character worried about school occasionally

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried
Tiny Tim is a character in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A small figure is anxious about going to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny character' looks like a small letter, but it is Tiny Tim from Dickens's A Christmas Carol; 'about' wraps the worry around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done now and then happens occasionally, a straight adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Oddly unplanned lumps on this — honestly!

indicators.note: oddly says to take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: An exclamation of exasperation at lumpy, unplanned bumps on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the two words as one string: the odd letters spell it out. 'on this' completes the idiom: on the ___ means honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on the ___' means honest or legitimate, so with on this it says honestly.

clue.text: Clean out dungeon with a common acid

indicators.note: cleaning out the word removes all its insides, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrub a dungeon using an everyday acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean out' empties DUNGEON to its first and last letters, D and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Deoxyribonucleic acid, carrier of genes, is present in nearly every living cell, so it is very common.

clue.text: Limit quantities of celebs such as Descartes

parts.note: to ration is to limit the quantities of something
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A call to cap the number of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Descartes was the leading philosopher of the school holding that reason, not the senses, is the source of knowledge.

clue.text: This herb, it could identify a nation

indicators.note: could suggests the letters might be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A herb, it is suggested, could mark out a particular nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' signals rearranging THIS HERB IT; 'identify' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of the United Kingdom, taken together, form a nation.

clue.text: Certain pay-off, whatever you offer

indicators.note: off means the letters of certain pay are not right, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A guaranteed payout, no matter what is bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay-off' reads as one word, but 'off' is the anagram signal on CERTAIN PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless of cost, so whatever price is offered.

clue.text: Turn brown before dance

indicators.note: before places the colour ahead of the turn

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Getting a suntan before going out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn brown' looks like one verb, but the two words are separate pieces, with 'before' putting the colour first.
explanation.definitionFit: This Argentine ballroom dance is a familiar example of a dance.

clue.text: Sees club putting up screen positions

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means reading the letters upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to spot is to see
a bat is a club used in games

explanation.surface: Someone notices a club erecting a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Tab stops are the preset positions on a computer screen where text lines up when tabbing.

clue.text: Peron's space walk

definitions.meaning: ... Peron, wife of Argentina's President Juan Peron
extravehicular activity, NASA's abbreviation for an astronaut working outside the craft

explanation.surface: The Argentine first lady takes a stroll in space.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both Evita Peron's first name and the space agency abbreviation for extravehicular activity.

clue.text: Once more in contact with missing saint

indicators.note: missing says the saint is lost from the longer word

parts.note: leaning against something is being in contact with it

explanation.surface: Back in touch with somebody, without a saint this time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more is doing it a second time, a straight adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Enjoyably odd account starts to inform

indicators.note: starts means the account comes at the start

parts.note: quaint means charmingly or enjoyably old-fashioned and odd

explanation.surface: A charmingly strange report begins to inform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' reads as begins to, but 'starts' puts AC first.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone familiar with facts is to inform them of those facts.

clue.text: Need French papers' answer in times of financial crisis

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the multiplication word

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in four by three
need means lack
identity papers are ID

explanation.surface: Wanting French papers to answer during periods of financial distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' is the maths sense: BY. The first Black Friday was the 1869 crash of the US gold market.
explanation.definitionFit: Several stock and gold market panics, notably in 1869, earned this name, a day of financial crisis.

clue.text: Executioner initially appalled by up-and-coming celeb

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of appalled

parts.note: by means times in maths, written as the multiplication sign x

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: An executioner is shocked by a rising star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-and-coming' looks like promising but reverses NAME; 'by' is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsman who executes with an axe is an executioner.

clue.text: Subdued muscle- bound woman

indicators.note: bound means the muscle wraps around the woman

parts.note: quad is short for quadriceps, the thigh muscle
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A muscle-bound woman is overpowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muscle-bound' reads as one word, but split it: 'bound' makes the thigh muscle wrap around the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed or put down, as a rebellion is, means subdued.

clue.text: Primeval energy found in American heavy metal

indicators.note: found in says energy is placed inside the metal

parts.note: gold is a dense, heavy metal
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Ancient energy is discovered in an American heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' suggests the music; here it is the dense element GOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something primeval dates from the earliest ages, so it is extremely ancient.

clue.text: River very fashionable for a drive?

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
hot means very fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy river setting chosen for a car trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests motoring; in golf a drive is the long opening shot off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the opening stroke from the tee is usually a drive, hit with the driver club.

clue.text: Caught socks in gardens

indicators.note: caught as in heard, so the word for socks is taken by ear

parts.note: hose is an old word for socks and stockings

explanation.surface: Somebody is caught with socks in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To garden is to work the soil, and weeding with a blade on a long handle is gardening.

clue.text: Family handle one leaving South American country

indicators.note: leaving says the one departs from the country's name

parts.note: Suriname is a country on the north coast of South America
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A family manages someone departing a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a name, and 'Family handle' is one's family name.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name, and the name shared by a family is the last name.

clue.text: See 23
See 1
Returning god is able to half- seal waterway

indicators.note: returning means the god's name comes back reversed

parts.note: Zeus is the chief Greek god
can means is able to

indicators.note: half takes the second half of the word seal

explanation.surface: A god coming back can partly seal off a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian canal linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea is a famous artificial waterway.
